Subject: Order form + MSA redlines — output & training

Hi Irene,

Attached are Acme's annotated redlines to the proposed Order Form and the MSA exhibit. The commercial terms look fine, but legal has several concerns around three IP-related items that need explicit language before procurement can run the PO:

1) Output ownership / productization: Acme is asking for assignment of output rights for models trained on Acme prompts/data. We need to understand Redwood's standard approach and whether an assignment is required or if a license suffices.

2) Training / data use: Redlines currently seek a blanket prohibition on using customer data for training. Please confirm whether Redwood can provide an operational opt-out (per-customer flag) and what controls/assurances accompany that.

3) Feedback & telemetry: Legal wants to limit any perpetual license for feedback to operational improvements and exclude commercialization. Also asking about telemetry retention and whether telemetry is considered customer content.

Can you route this to the right internal owners? We've labeled comments inline (see Attachment). We'd like a short call next week if needed — procurement is aiming to sign by 2/14.

Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_redlines_20280202.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Maria Garza
Chief Legal Officer

Subject: Proposed responses — Output / Training / Feedback (DEAL-ACM-2028-047)

Maria — following our internal sync, we dug into Acme's redlines and have a proposed middle ground. High level answers first, then annotated language in the attached doc (Redwood_response_annotated_20280204.docx).

High level proposals:
- Output ownership: Redwood cannot assign title to model outputs or models themselves. We can offer an exclusive-enough commercial license for Acme's internal productization (including incorporation into Acme's customer-facing features) for a defined set of outputs/use cases. For clarity: this would be a worldwide, perpetual, non-transferable license to use outputs generated from Acme-supplied prompts/data for Acme's products; Redwood retains all model code and model-level IP.

- Training / data use: Redwood can provide a per-customer opt-out for training (opt-out flag at account level) that prevents using customer prompts/content for future model training and weight updates. We propose operational safeguards: timestamps/audit logs showing opt-out enforcement, and an SLA window for opt-out propagation (up to 48 hours). We cannot retroactively remove content from models once ingested into a public training sweep prior to opt-out (we will flag that in the doc).

- Feedback license & telemetry: Redwood can accept a limited feedback license solely for improving Redwood's service (bug fixes, latency, internal quality). We are unwilling to grant Acme rights to commercialize aggregated telemetry as an output of Redwood IP. Telemetry will be treated as operational metadata (retention policy 90 days by default; enterprise retention available as an add-on).

Next steps we propose:
1) Please review the attached tracked-change language — Jordan/Kimberly drafted conservative responses that implement the above.
2) If Acme is aligned on the license approach, we can mark the Order Form with a productization license exhibit and deliver an SOW-like annex enumerating the exact permitted uses.
3) Schedule a 30-min legal + product call this week to settle remaining punts (transferability, escrow, attribution).

Attachment: Redwood_response_annotated_20280204.docx (docx)

If useful, Ben can join the call to run through how the opt-out works and the propagation SLA. Proposed times: Tue 2/7 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 2/8 13:00-13:30 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
